newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 31.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has come under heavy fire from democracy groups for granting a pension to Colonel Narong Kittikachorn who was dismissed from service for his role in the bloody suppression of protesters in the 1973 October 14 uprising. Gen Chavalit has approved the pension for Col Narong in June last year while serving as defence minister in the Banharn Silpa-archa administration. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- A manhunt has been launched to round up more than 50 detainees who escaped from a cell at a police station in Nakhon Pathom province. A police committee has also been set up to investigate the incident and those found responsible will be punished. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Although the Maung Thong Thani housing estate in Nonthaburi province is still the main option for the new parliament building, residents there are opposed to the scheme, claiming it will be detrimental to their livelihoods. A resident says the housing estate is not suitable for a national institution such as the parliament. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT) is studying whether to widen its business to include telephone and other services using fibre-optic cables. The authority can provide these services when the telecommunications industry is liberalised. The cables could be laid alongside the EGAT's power transmission network nationwide. (BANGKOK POST)

- Some foreign countries will take their bilateral aviation disputes with the Aviation Department to governmental dialogues for settlement if the open sky policy continues to be neglected. The Netherlands has sent an official letter to the Foreign Ministry after it failed to reach a bilateral aviation agreement on third and fourth freedom rights. (THE NATION)
